title: Mini-session priority grouper to reduce KV spike risk in streaming chat
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Design and implement a lightweight session-level grouping heuristic ("mini-session priority grouper") to form continuous micro-batches for streaming chat that reduce KV cache churn and avoid GPU memory spike events without meaningfully increasing p95 latency.

Background: Our streaming chat workload shows transient hot-spots when many cold sessions simultaneously produce turns with long prefixes. Those events cause KV cache fills and occasional GPU memory pressure that triggers eviction thrashing or temporary OOMs on smaller slabs. Existing batchers are good at steady-state throughput but do not prioritize avoiding high-amplitude KV write bursts.

Success criteria (target):
- Reduce 99th-percentile per-GPU peak KV memory delta during 1-hour synthetic stress runs by >= 25%.
- Keep streaming p95 latency regression < 5% compared to current baseline.
- No more than 5% reduction in overall token throughput under long-tail workloads.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Must operate with very low CPU overhead (<2% of batcher CPU budget).
- Can't require model changes or per-customer coordination during rollout.
- Fairness: priority grouping may increase latency for some low-activity sessions; we cap per-session deprioritization windows to avoid user-visible regressions.
proposed_solution:
Introduce a compact per-session 'mini-session' metadata record (last_active_ts, recent_turn_tokens, priority_score) kept in the batcher's in-memory index. When a streaming turn arrives we compute a transient priority score: priority = alpha * recency_factor + beta * session_size_score + gamma * customer_tier_adjustment. The batcher then groups ready tokens into micro-batches using a two-pass formation: (1) form a latency-first queue for high-priority sessions (low recent_turn_tokens and high recency); (2) fill remaining batch slots with lower-priority sessions but enforce a soft token slab reservation (soft_reserve_tokens) that caps how many cold-session tokens can enter a single batch to limit simultaneous KV growth.

We also add a small background 'cooldown' sampler that proactively schedules one token from long-dormant sessions into periodic mini-batches to warm KV entries gradually rather than in a single spike. Cooldown frequency is adaptive based on current GPU KV pressure metrics (kv_fill_rate, kv_eviction_rate).

Implementation notes: keep metadata in the same epoch-sharded in-memory map used by the existing planner to avoid serialization overhead. Expose two new tuning knobs: soft_reserve_tokens_per_batch and cooldown_rate_per_slot. Provide defaults targeted at the 4-GPU slab sizes used in Dedicated small instances.
decisions: Use lightweight in-band metadata in batcher rather than centralized store to minimize latency and lock contention
Prefer soft reservations to strict hard reservations to maintain throughput under load
Cooldown sampler will be reactive and tied to KV pressure signals rather than fixed timers
No model-level instrumentation; all heuristics live in serving runtime to simplify rollout and rollback
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Spike analysis completed — reproduced KV memory spike in lab using synthetic mix (30% long-prefix chat; 70% short-turn). Identified root cause as simultaneous KV allocate spikes when many cold sessions had first long turns.
2026-02-20: Prototype grouping algorithm implemented in batcher simulator (python). Local runs indicate ~18% reduction in peak KV delta with alpha/beta/gamma = 0.6/0.3/0.1 and soft_reserve_tokens=64.
2026-02-27: Converted prototype to Rust planner hook. Added mini-session metadata with epoch sharding. Initial integration tests passed in CI (unit + integration).

2026-03-03: Canary on internal staging: synthetic 10k concurrent sessions. Observed p95 latency +2.8%, p99 KV peak -22%. Noted higher latency for certain churny low-priority sessions — added fairness cap to deprioritization window.
2026-03-08: Implemented adaptive cooldown sampler tied to kv_eviction_rate metric. Reduced cold-session latency regressions in staging by ~40% compared to initial canary.
2026-03-10: Code review comments addressed; preparing PR for runtime-1.21. Added docs for two new knobs and default values for 4-GPU and 8-GPU configs.
test_results: Baseline (no grouping): synthetic mix peak KV delta = 3.2 GB per GPU; streaming p95 = 110 ms; throughput = 100k tokens/s
Staging (mini-session grouping + soft_reserve_tokens=64): peak KV delta = 2.48 GB per GPU (-22.5%); streaming p95 = 113 ms (+2.7%); throughput = 98.9k tokens/s (-1.1%)
With adaptive cooldown enabled: peak KV delta = 2.2 GB per GPU (-31% vs baseline); streaming p95 = 115 ms (+4.5%); observed fewer OOM incidents in long-tail stress runs
